implementation: One temporary DTW context per pass, closed in finally; identical model, clips, decoding parameters and acceptance rules.
Last decoded recording retained only in RAM as an immutable copy, capped at 8 MiB. Existing per-job file PCM is reused for larger recordings.
PCM key includes audio and model metadata; deletion, encryption, wipe and stale-writer revisions invalidate it.
Completed boundary words retain the text they were checked against; a changed local text requests that clip again and leaves other completed clips cached.
device_tests: independent versus reused contexts: exact native words/probabilities/times and speaker labels match
full repair followed by one invalidated clip using RAM PCM: passed; full saved segments and labels unchanged
unchanged repeat skips local inference: passed
limitations: Single local recording and sequential measurements, not a general speed or DER benchmark.
The isolated context comparison measured 47.179 s versus 40.595 s. Another full job measured 61.3 s; do not promise a fixed speedup.
The 25.978 s partial repair performs one clip, so it is not an equal-work comparison against the full pass.
RAM PCM is lost on process exit and is not retained for recordings larger than 8 MiB decoded. No decoded audio is newly persisted.
Audio, transcript, database and embeddings stay local; only anonymous counts/timings are included.
Installed diagnostic APK uses preinstalled phone models.
